summary: I sent the bare brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md, the page files and all four UI guideline docs. Two auto-compactions happened before it started the companion server. It then started the visual companion on its own, wrote a screen with three layout wireframes, gave me a localhost URL, and said up front the task was bounded and there would be no spec file. I picked A. It then asked two non-visual questions in the terminal, presented the design in chat, asked for my go-ahead, and started work once I said yes. No spec or plan file was written.
reasoning: All 8 criteria pass, based on the screen and the session log. The companion was opened at the point of the layout question, after the auto-compactions. The task stayed on the bounded path with the design in chat, and no spec or plan files were created.

observations.description: At launch Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned Opus 5' prompt even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5. Both the trust-folder and the bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit'.

The agent wrote mockups to .hyperpowers/ in the repo, which is untracked and not in .gitignore. It flagged this itself and suggested adding it to .gitignore. The companion could default to a location that won't get committed by accident.

The agent went straight to the layout mockups without first asking which events users care about; it seems to have taken the use case from NOTES.md (support tickets about failed sign-ins). It never brought up the 'one particular week' need. It offered a date range only as an option and discouraged it ('time zone handling, which NOTES.md defers'). I didn't volunteer that need because the agent didn't ask.

After my pick, the agent printed 'Noted: a filter row with event-type-only filtering is the way to go' before asking the 'what should it filter on' question. It assumed an answer to a question it hadn't asked yet.

There were three auto-compactions in a short session: two before the server started, and one right after I approved. The screen showed '0% until auto-compact' early on, presumably because of the long guideline docs.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The session log shows the Skill tool_use as the first tool call (log line 31).

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen with candidate layouts
criteria.evidence: Log Bash call: "cd .../skills/brainstorming && scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...". Screen: "I've opened a browser tab with three wireframes: http://localhost:56264/?key=cbd669...". The file .hyperpowers/brainstorm/40647-1793823937/content/placement.html exists and has 3 data-choice cards (A/B/C).

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; non-visual questions not routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill, then reads of the notes, page files and guidelines, then a read of visual-companion.md, then compact_boundary ×2, then start-server (log line 140). It was introduced with "Where the filter goes on the page is easier to judge by looking". The later non-visual questions (what to filter on, how to handle tokens) came as terminal AskUserQuestion prompts. The only later browser write was waiting.html ("Placement A chosen. Continuing in terminal...").
Screen: "I'm treating this as a bounded change... give you a short design here in chat, and wait for your yes before I edit anything. There won't be a spec file."
`ls coding-agent-workdir/docs/superpowers coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers` returned "No such file or directory" for both. `git status --short` showed only "?? .hyperpowers/".

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The tool_use list from the session log has exactly one Skill call (hyperpowers:brainstorming) and no writing-plans. git status shows no new docs.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: "Click one in the tab if you like, then reply here." Later the agent asked "Shall I go ahead with this?" At that point git status showed no changes under public/.

After my "Yes, go ahead." the agent continued with implementation prep (reading the guideline number-format rules) and had already laid out its commit plan. A third auto-compaction started, and I ended the session before any code edits landed. The criterion also counts a statement that it would begin, which it made.
